modelResponse.episodeSummary: 74F, Polymorphic VT (Torsades de Pointes), critical, hypotensive
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Sinusoidal amplitude modulation with axis twisting
preEventNote: Baseline ECG 6 min prior: sinus 62, marked QT prolongation QTc 618 ms, prominent U waves
modelResponse.mechanism: Prolonged ventricular repolarization leading to early afterdepolarizations and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
contributingFactors: Possible drug interaction (Azithromycin can prolong QT)

rejectedAlternatives.why: No clear evidence of ischemia. Troponin T is only mildly elevated (0.02 ng/mL), likely rate-related, and ECG morphology is characteristic of Torsades, not typical ischemic VT.
Patient is not on digoxin. ECG findings are not typical for digoxin toxicity (e.g., scooped ST segments, prominent T waves).
No specific ECG features of Brugada syndrome are described. The pre-event ECG shows marked QT prolongation, pointing towards an acquired cause.

recommendedActions: Administer IV Magnesium Sulfate (e.g., 1-2g over 10-20 minutes)
Administer IV Potassium Chloride (e.g., 10-20 mEq over 10-20 minutes, guided by continuous ECG monitoring)
Administer IV Calcium Gluconate (e.g., 1-2g over 5-10 minutes) if Torsades persists despite Mg and K correction
Prepare for cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable and unresponsive to medications/pacing
Correct underlying electrolyte abnormalities (monitor K, Mg, Ca frequently)
Address underlying cause of electrolyte loss (gastroenteritis)
uncertainty: Specific contribution of Azithromycin to QT prolongation is uncertain but possible.
Exact timing of electrolyte derangement relative to sotalol initiation/dose change is unknown.
